verdicts.why: Ramonda calls Killmonger a liar and is convinced when W'Kabi hands her the royal ring N'Jadaka carried; Erik does not produce it himself.
Ramonda says T'Chaka's spirit is with them when she greets T'Challa on his return home, before the coronation; at the ceremony she only urges him to show M'Baku who he is.
T'Chaka sending Okoye on T'Challa's 2008 mission comes only from the Black Panther Prelude comic; the film shows no such scene, so the cut text is accurate.

T'Challa captures Zemo in Civil War and Zemo is handed to Ross, who holds and taunts him; Ross also meets T'Challa at the Berlin task force. Black Panther only refers back to it, so the split keeps the Busan, Wakanda and Killmonger facts.
Yelena first appears in Hawkeye episode 4, ambushing Clint at Maya's building until he unmasks her and she flees; the near-kill and truce over Natasha come in episode 6.

value.title: The Falcon and the Winter Soldier#3
value.text: Sharon Carter, living as a fugitive in Madripoor, shelters Bucky, Sam and Zemo and helps them track the serum.
value.on_a_card_about_b: Shelters Bucky, Sam and Zemo in Madripoor and helps track the serum.
value.on_b_card_about_a: A guest Sharon shelters in Madripoor.

split.title: The Falcon and the Winter Soldier#6
split.text: Sharon joins Bucky and Sam in New York against the Flag Smashers. All the while she is secretly running Madripoor as the Power Broker.
split.on_a_card_about_b: Shelters Bucky, Sam and Zemo in Madripoor and helps track the serum. Secretly the Power Broker.
split.on_b_card_about_a: A guest Sharon shelters in Madripoor while secretly ruling it as the Power Broker.

verdicts.why: Sharon first appears in episode 3, so #3 is right, but she is only revealed as the Power Broker in episode 6 (to Batroc), so that fact moves to a split at #6.

value.title: The Falcon and the Winter Soldier#3
value.text: Years later she helps Zemo, Sam and Bucky in Madripoor, the city run by the Power Broker.
value.on_a_card_about_b: Ally in Madripoor, the city of the Power Broker.

split.title: The Falcon and the Winter Soldier#6
split.text: Sharon is revealed to be the Power Broker herself, secretly ruling the city where she helped Zemo.
split.on_a_card_about_b: Ally in Madripoor, secretly the Power Broker Zemo warns of.
split.on_b_card_about_a: Baron Sharon helps in Madripoor while secretly ruling it as the Power Broker.

verdicts.why: Zemo is freed and meets Sharon in Madripoor in episode 3, so #3 is right, but her identity as the Power Broker is revealed only in episode 6, so it goes in a split.
Sharon only suspects the interrogator once the power cuts out; she then leads Stark and Romanoff to the rampaging Bucky and is thrown onto a table. She never confronts Zemo.

Civil War shows Ayo travelling with T'Chaka and T'Challa to Vienna, not T'Chaka recruiting her. Her line that he 'chose me to protect him' comes only later, in The Falcon and the Winter Soldier#4, so dropping it from this stage is right.

Sam asks Dunphy for an update when he finds Sidewinder, but Sidewinder ambushes Sam and Sam beats him at a salvage yard; Dunphy then holds him at the Norfolk SEAL facility. The film calls the group Serpent, not the Serpent Society.

value.text: Peggy Carter fights HYDRA with the SSR, and Arnim Zola is its leading scientist. After Steve's team captures Zola on his train, his interrogation leads Peggy and the SSR to the Red Skull's last base.

verdicts.why: The drugging at Castle Kaufmann is from the First Vengeance comic only. In the film Zola's intel leads to the last HYDRA base. HYDRA is Schmidt's group, not 'Zola's', so the first sentence is corrected.

value.text: Natasha meets T'Challa in Vienna, and after his father is killed she tells him the task force will decide who brings in the killer, but he vows to kill him himself. At the airport battle, she turns on Tony's side and stuns T'Challa so Steve and Bucky can escape.
value.on_a_card_about_b: Wakanda's prince. Natasha consoles him in Vienna, then stuns him at the airport.
value.on_b_card_about_a: An Avenger who consoles T'Challa in Vienna, then stuns him at the airport.

verdicts.why: There is no promise of justice; her line is 'Task Force will decide who brings in Barnes', and he answers that he will kill him himself. The proposal's 'will bring in the killer' is corrected to match.
Sitwell is a hostage in the Lemurian Star's galley ('One officer, Jasper Sitwell'), and STRIKE frees him during Steve's mission. He is not part of the rescue team.
Carol overpowers Starforce, Att-Lass and Bron-Char among them, at Mar-Vell's laboratory in Earth's orbit. The only Kree she fights on the ground is Yon-Rogg.
Korath and Bron-Char fight Carol in the orbiting Mar-Vell laboratory battle, not on Earth.
In 1995 the S.H.I.E.L.D. team is led by Director Keller (impersonated by Talos); Fury is a field agent and Coulson a new agent working with him, so 'director' is wrong.
In Lagos Rumlow fights Natasha and Steve, while Sam hunts his armored truck from the air until Rumlow has his men ditch it and scatter. Sam and Rumlow never fight each other.
G'iah uses the Harvest and gains the heroes' powers only in the finale, episode 6 ('Home'), where she poses as Fury and kills Gravik.

In episode 1 Fury returns and teams with Talos, who tells him the Skrulls are angry that they still have no home and that Fury disappeared. Gravik kills Talos while Fury pulls Ritson out in episode 4, so the death goes in the split.
Sam and Bucky are apart in episode 1 and first team up against the Flag Smashers in Munich in episode 2. They fix the boat and agree to move on and work together in episode 5.
In Into the Ring the masked man has already hit the Russians' operation; Anatoly and Vladimir discuss him with Wesley and kidnap a boy to trap him. The conflict starts in episode 1.
Ben and Blake's only scene together is the episode 6 ('Condemned') warehouse standoff, where Blake mocks him and says 'The world's a shitty place. You can quote me.'

Karen first asks Ben for help in episode 3. In episode 4 he coaches her at the Union Allied auction and the diner, and they keep working together after that. In episode 12 she gets him to write the story and Fisk kills him.

Matt is introduced to Ben at the Nelson and Murdock office in episode 9, where the group starts working against Fisk; Fisk kills Ben in episode 12. Ben's episode 8 meeting is with the masked man, not with Matt the lawyer.
In episode 9 Ben and the others start digging into Fisk's past. Ben and Karen visit Fisk's mother in episode 10, and Fisk learns of it and kills Ben in episode 12.

Manning has no contact with Poindexter in S3#5; there he only pulls the file that Fisk reads. Manning first handles him in S3#6, collecting him and delivering the Daredevil suit for the Bulletin attack.
In S3#6 Poindexter, dressed as Daredevil, attacks the Bulletin, fights off Matt and kills Evans. The Clinton Church fight is S3#10.

In Born Again S2#4 Daredevil stops Fisk from killing the wounded Dex at Fogwell's Gym and they escape together. The custody (#5), Soledad's treatment (#6) and the release to protect McCaffrey (#7) all come later.
Poindexter only meets Fisk as an FBI agent in S3#2. Fisk wins him over and sends him out in the Daredevil suit in S3#6, and Fisk breaks his back at the wedding in S3#13.
In S3#6 Poindexter attacks the Bulletin to kill Jasper Evans before he can talk. When Ellison blocks his path, Poindexter strikes him down. He goes after Karen later, at Clinton Church.
Nadeem works out in S3#8 that Poindexter is the attacker and searches his apartment with Matt. Poindexter comes home, wounds him, and tells Fisk that Nadeem knows. He kills Nadeem in S3#12.

value.title: Daredevil S3#9
value.text: Benjamin Poindexter, a friend from Ray's work, visits the Nadeem home, and Seema makes him eggs while he quietly threatens Ray.
value.on_a_card_about_b: Ray's wife, who welcomes Poindexter as a family friend.
value.on_b_card_about_a: A family friend from Ray's work, who visits to threaten Ray.

split.title: Daredevil S3#12
split.on_a_card_about_b: Ray's wife. Poindexter kills her husband.
split.on_b_card_about_a: A former family friend who kills Seema's husband.

verdicts.why: S3#9 is the first episode where Seema and Poindexter meet: she welcomes him and makes him eggs, and he kills Ray in S3#12. At #9 Seema treats him as a family friend, so the kind for that stage becomes friend, not enemy.
In S3#2 Hattley assigns Nadeem, Poindexter and FBI SWAT to escort Fisk to the hotel. In S3#4 she hears Poindexter may have lied in his report and meets Nadeem and Winn about it.

value.title: Daredevil S2#2
value.on_b_card_about_a: A prosecutor who sometimes opposes and sometimes helps Matt.

split.title: Daredevil S3#12
split.text: Now District Attorney, Tower agrees to let Matt and Foggy's client Ray Nadeem testify against Fisk before a grand jury.
split.on_a_card_about_b: A lawyer whose firm Tower sometimes opposes, sometimes helps.
split.on_b_card_about_a: A prosecutor, later DA, who sometimes opposes and sometimes helps Matt.

verdicts.why: Tower first appears in S2#2, dealing with Nelson and Murdock over Grotto, so the move is right. He becomes DA only after Reyes's death, and in Daredevil he is first shown as DA with Matt in S3#12, so 'later DA' moves to a split there.

value.title: Daredevil S2#2
value.text: Blake Tower serves under District Attorney Samantha Reyes, and they use Grotto as bait to catch the Punisher.

split.title: Daredevil S2#10
split.text: Tower is with Reyes when she is shot dead in her office.
split.on_a_card_about_b: Tower's boss, the DA, shot dead in front of him.
split.on_b_card_about_a: A prosecutor under Reyes, with her when she is shot dead.

split.title: Luke Cage S1#11
split.text: After Reyes's death, Tower succeeds her as District Attorney.
split.on_a_card_about_b: Tower's late boss, the DA he succeeds.
split.on_b_card_about_a: A prosecutor under Reyes, who succeeds her as DA.

verdicts.why: Tower works under Reyes on the Grotto sting from S2#2, and Reyes is shot in front of him in S2#10. At #10 he has not succeeded her: he plans to leave town and is first shown as DA in Luke Cage S1#11, so 'succeeds' needs its own split.
Mahoney checks Hoffman's bag and lets him into Blake's room in S1#8. Daredevil sends Hoffman to turn himself in to Mahoney in S1#13.
Mahoney is already on the case at the Burren Club in S2#1, telling Foggy and Matt that the killings are a targeted, military-trained assault. He takes the credit for Castle's arrest in S2#4.

value.title: Daredevil S2#2
value.text: Brett Mahoney looks after Grotto at the precinct when the Punisher marks him, laying out his options and urging him to take the DA's witness protection deal.
value.on_a_card_about_b: A marked man Mahoney urges to take witness protection.
value.on_b_card_about_a: The cop who tries to protect Grotto from the Punisher.

split.title: Daredevil S2#3
split.text: The Punisher gets to Grotto anyway and kills him.
split.on_a_card_about_b: A marked man Mahoney could not protect.
split.on_b_card_about_a: The cop who tried to protect Grotto from the Punisher.

verdicts.why: Mahoney's scene with Grotto is at the precinct in S2#2, and Grotto dies in S2#3. Mahoney never puts Grotto into witness protection: he says the DA is sending people about it and urges him to take the deal, so the text and card are corrected.
The arrest happens in S1#13: Mahoney finds Fisk beaten by the man in the red suit and handcuffs him.
Hoffman turns himself in and hires Matt and Foggy as his lawyers in S1#13. Foggy's only earlier contact with him is the S1#1 confrontation over Karen's release, which is not this relationship.
